task: TASTE (gustatory) transduction CERT: (1) sweet+umami via T1R GPCR heterodimers (T1R2+T1R3 sweet, T1R1+T1R3 umami) -> gustducin -> PLCbeta2 -> IP3 -> TRPM5 -> depolarization -> CALHM1 ATP release; (2) bitter via ~25 T2Rs -> SAME downstream cascade; (3) salt via ENaC (amiloride-sensitive, appetitive low-salt) + high-salt co-opting bitter/sour pathways (amiloride-insensitive, aversive); (4) sour via OTOP1 proton channel in Type III cells. FALSIFIER: the decisive genetic double/triple-dissociation (TRPM5/PLCbeta2/CALHM1-KO abolish sweet+umami+bitter, spare sour+salt; OTOP1-KO abolishes sour; ENaC-KO abolishes salt-appetitive) must fall a 'single universal taste receptor' adversary. Concentration->intensity dose-response per modality. Labeled-line vs across-fiber-pattern coding held OPEN (not adjudicated).

symmetric_qc_open_items: AUDITABLE CORRECTION 1: the task's pre-registered 'T1R3-KO must abolish sweet+umami' is FALSIFIED AS LITERALLY STATED by Damak et al 2003's own primary data -- the measured result is 'diminished but not abolished' (full abolition only for the artificial-sweetener subset). The 'single universal receptor' adversary is NOT rescued by this: the residual response is explained by a SECOND named, modality-specific mechanism (taste-mGluR4 for umami), which is MORE modality-specific structure, not less. Reported precisely rather than silently matching the task's stated threshold.

AUDITABLE CORRECTION 2: the task's framing of an 'amiloride-insensitive aversive high-salt path' (worded as if a third, dedicated salt-specific sensor) is refined by Oka et al 2013's own data: high salt does not activate a separate salt-specific aversive receptor -- it CROSS-ACTIVATES the pre-existing bitter- and sour-sensing cells/pathways. Reported as a correction, not smoothed into the task's original wording.

G1's block-contrast is only 2-sided (both blocks measured in the SAME paper) for 3 of 7 rows (TRPM5/PLCbeta2, CALHM1, Gustducin). The other 4 rows (T1R3, OTOP1, ENaCalpha, Oka-silencing) each report only their OWN affected modality in their own abstract -- coded as honest NA, not fabricated as 'normal', for the untested side. General cross-modality separateness for those is supported only indirectly, by Chandrashekar 2010's own general statement that the other 4 modalities are mediated by separate dedicated TRC populations -- a citation of a claim, not this session's own measurement of those specific KOs' cross-modality effects.

G2's redundancy/branching-factor model is a STRUCTURAL CONSISTENCY check, not an independent blind prediction: the branching factor b for Gustducin and T1R3 was read from the SAME source papers' own discussion of alternate pathways (rod transducin; taste-mGluR4), so a concordant result is partly expected given correct reading of the source, not a fully out-of-sample forecast. Disclosed, not oversold, mirroring the gate-strength-tiering discipline used in docs/MECHANISM_OLFACTORY_TRANSDUCTION.md.

G4's 'naive uniform coverage' null (3/25=12%) is an order-of-magnitude back-of-envelope comparator, not a rigorously derived null distribution over receptor-compound bipartite coverage (compounds can be detected by multiple receptors simultaneously, so a simple linear-partition null is a simplification, disclosed as such).

G5 (psychophysics) uses only 2 of Mojet et al 2001's 10 tested compounds' fold-changes (the two named in the abstract, aspartame and IMP) -- the other 8 and the absolute mM threshold concentrations were NOT fetched (full text not retrieved this session); NOT gated PASS/FAIL for this reason, reported as descriptive only.

Finger et al 2005 (ATP/P2X2/P2X3 afferent step) -- bibliographic identity (title/PMID/DOI/journal/authors) verified live; the SPECIFIC quantitative impairment (% reduction in CT/glossopharyngeal nerve response in P2X2/P2X3 double-KO) was not independently re-extracted from full text this session, disclosed not fabricated.

The labeled-line vs across-fiber-pattern coding debate is HELD OPEN by explicit task instruction (G6) -- Mueller 2005 and Wu 2015 are reported as two genuine, non-contradicted anchors on different sides/aspects of the question; this doc does not adjudicate it.

No independent re-derivation of the CALHM1 percentage-impairment magnitude or the ENaC-KO's quantitative (vs qualitative 'complete loss') behavioral preference-score reduction was attempted this session -- both are reported at the qualitative/categorical level the source abstracts themselves state.

The NHANES CSX_H gLMS quinine-intensity distribution was checked for a taster/non-taster bimodal signature (motivated by the TAS2R38 genetics) and found INCONCLUSIVE from summary statistics alone (mean 53.2, median 52.0, sd 22.7 -- no visible bimodality without genotype data or a proper multimodality test); NOT pursued further or claimed as evidence, an honest dead end disclosed rather than forced into a claim.
